notes: GAAP village. Governmental: Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances (p5), Total column. Fund balance roll: 564,318 + 712,680 - 771,536 + 139,725 - 12,925 + 1,400 (proceeds from sale of equipment, in other_financing) - 644 (correction of error) = 633,018. Business-type: Statement of Revenues, Expenses and Changes in Net Position (p8-p9), Total column of the Business-Type Activities (Electric, Water, Sewer, nonmajor Garbage). The statement has no single total revenue or expense line, so receipts = operating revenues 855,527 + nonoperating revenues (interest 3,797, misc 5,439, intergovernmental 17,182, gain on sale 1,545) and disbursements = operating expenses 786,175 + interest expense 7,569; net position 182,512 + 883,490 - 793,744 - 126,800 transfers - 14,663 correction of error = 130,795. Business-type operating expense lines are the Total column (p9) and include a Garbage fund; cost-type lines carry the cost type as category with function utilities (re-check 2026-10-28: 'Gas, Oil, Propane' 4,345 recategorized from utilities to Fuel). Governmental ending_cash = cash 7,667 + CDs 1,351 from the governmental funds balance sheet (p4). Balance sheet: government-wide Statement of Net Position (p1), Total primary government column; Internal Balances show 564,226 in governmental and -564,226 in business-type and net to zero in the Total column (not itemized). Compensated absences classified as accrued liabilities. Detail: only the budget comparison schedules (General p12, Economic Development Sales Tax and Street p13) which are on a budgetary basis and so differ from the GAAP fund statements (e.g. General revenue 462,955 vs 491,824 GAAP); Debt service lines on the General Fund. Pages: trimmed p1 report p4, p2-p3 report pp5-6 (activities split across two pages), p4 report p7, p5 report p9, p6-p7 report pp11-12, p8-p9 report pp13-14, p10-p11 report pp15-16, p12-p13 report pp29-30.
